extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors reporting animal experiments; peer reviewers and journal editors
extracted.subtask_description: A manuscript author checklist (ARRIVE 2.0) for reporting in vivo animal experiments to ensure transparency, reproducibility, and assessable reliability of findings. Intended to guide what information to include in manuscripts and for reviewers/editors to check.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment, provide brief details of study design including: a. The groups being compared, including control groups. If no control group has been used, the rationale should be stated. b. The experimental unit (e.g. a single animal, litter, or cage of animals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the 'Essential 10' basic minimum information required for assessing reliability. Should allow readers/reviewers to understand the comparisons and the unit of analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Specify the exact number of experimental units allocated to each group, and the total number in each experiment. Also indicate the total number of animals used. b. Explain how the sample size was decided. Provide details of any a priori sample size calculation, if done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report both group-level and experiment-level counts and justify sample size decisions; include power or other a priori calculations when available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Describe any criteria used for including and excluding animals (or experimental units) during the experiment, and data points during the analysis. Specify if these criteria were established a priori. If no criteria were set, state this explicitly. b. For each experimental group, report any animals, experimental units or data points not included in the analysis and explain why. If there were no exclusions, state so. c. For each analysis, report the exact value of n in each experimental group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit any pre-specified or post-hoc inclusion/exclusion rules and report exclusions transparently with reasons and final n values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: a. State whether randomisation was used to allocate experimental units to control and treatment groups. If done, provide the method used to generate the randomisation sequence. b. Describe the strategy used to minimise potential confounders such as the order of treatments and measurements, or animal/cage location. If confounders were not controlled, state this explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare randomisation approaches and other strategies to control confounding; if omitted, explicitly state that no measures were taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe who was aware of the group allocation at the different stages of the experiment (during the allocation, the conduct of the experiment, the outcome assessment, and the data analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the extent and timing of blinding (allocation, conduct, assessment, analysis) so readers can assess risk of bias from unblinded procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Clearly define all outcome measures assessed (e.g. cell death, molecular markers, or behavioural changes). b. For hypothesis-testing studies, specify the primary outcome measure, i.e. the outcome measure that was used to determine the sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish primary versus secondary outcomes and ensure the primary outcome used for sample size/power justification is explicitly named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Provide details of the statistical methods used for each analysis, including software used. b. Describe any methods used to assess whether the data met the assumptions of the statistical approach, and what was done if the assumptions were not met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include analysis methods, software, assumption checks, and remedial steps when assumptions fail (e.g., transformations, non-parametric tests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Provide species-appropriate details of the animals used, including species, strain and substrain, sex, age or developmental stage, and, if relevant, weight. b. Provide further relevant information on the provenance of animals, health/immune status, genetic modification status, genotype, and any previous procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give sufficient biological and provenance detail so other researchers can evaluate applicability and replicate the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experimental group, including controls, describe the procedures in enough detail to allow others to replicate them, including: a. What was done, how it was done and what was used. b. When and how often. c. Where (including detail of any acclimatisation periods). d. Why (provide rationale for procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide procedural detail (materials, timing, frequency, location, acclimatisation) and rationale to enable reproducibility and understanding of interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: For each experiment conducted, including independent replications, report: a. Summary/descriptive statistics for each experimental group, with a measure of variability where applicable (e.g. mean and SD, or median and range). b. If applicable, the effect size with a confidence interval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report descriptive statistics and, where relevant, effect sizes with confidence intervals to convey magnitude and precision, for each experiment and replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an accurate summary of the research objectives, animal species, strain and sex, key methods, principal findings, and study conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the abstract contains the essential contextual elements (objectives, species/strain/sex, methods, key findings, conclusions) for quick appraisal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Include sufficient scientific background to understand the rationale and context for the study, and explain the experimental approach. b. Explain how the animal species and model used address the scientific objectives and, where appropriate, the relevance to human biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide rationale and context linking model choice to objectives and, when relevant, translational relevance to human biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly describe the research question, research objectives and, where appropriate, specific hypotheses being tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clear research questions/hypotheses and objectives so readers can judge alignment of design and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the name of the ethical review committee or equivalent that has approved the use of animals in this study, and any relevant licence or protocol numbers (if applicable). If ethical approval was not sought or granted, provide a justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report ethical approval details or justify absence of approval to demonstrate compliance with oversight and welfare standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide details of housing and husbandry conditions, including any environmental enrichment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include housing, husbandry, and enrichment details that may affect animal physiology or behavior and thus influence outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Describe any interventions or steps taken in the experimental protocols to reduce pain, suffering and distress. b. Report any expected or unexpected adverse events. c. Describe the humane endpoints established for the study, the signs that were monitored and the frequency of monitoring. If the study did not have humane endpoints, state this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail welfare-related interventions, adverse events, and predefined humane endpoints and monitoring to allow assessment of ethical conduct and potential impacts on data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation / scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Interpret the results, taking into account the study objectives and hypotheses, current theory and other relevant studies in the literature. b. Comment on the study limitations including potential sources of bias, limitations of the animal model, and imprecision associated with the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide balanced interpretation considering objectives, prior literature, limitations, biases, model constraints, and statistical imprecision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability / translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Comment on whether, and how, the findings of this study are likely to generalise to other species or experimental conditions, including any relevance to human biology (where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss external validity and translational considerations so readers can judge applicability of findings beyond the specific study context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement indicating whether a protocol (including the research question, key design features, and analysis plan) was prepared before the study, and if and where this protocol was registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare pre-study protocol registration (or absence) and provide registry details to support transparency and reduce selective reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement describing if and where study data are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State data availability and repositories/links if applicable to enable verification and reuse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: a. Declare any potential conflicts of interest, including financial and non-financial. If none exist, this should be stated. b. List all funding sources (including grant identifier) and the role of the funder(s) in the design, analysis and reporting of the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose conflicts and funding sources with grant identifiers and describe funders' roles to allow readers to assess potential influences on the research.
